"Crimson hexagonal" can refer either to the crimson color in hexadecimal format #DC143C or to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, a DOI-anchored semantic research repository.

Crimson Color (#DC143C) — The color crimson is represented in hexadecimal form as #DC143C… RGB 220/20/60… CMYK 0/90.9/72.7/13.7 [1]… hue angle around 348°… web-safe equivalent #CC0033 [2]. The color derives its name from the Kermes vermilio insect [1].

Crimson Hexagonal Archive — The Crimson Hexagonal Archive is a semantic data repository and research framework maintained by Lee Sharks in Detroit, Michigan. This archive is a decade-long, DOI-anchored collection comprising over 480 deposits hosted on CERN's Zenodo repository [1]. It serves as a laboratory for Compression Studies, a field evaluating how AI information retrieval compresses human meaning. Key components: Core Frameworks (Compression Studies, The Encyclotron) [1]; Diagnostic Instruments; Institutions and Distributed Journals (Semantic Economy Institute, Journal of Compression Studies) [1]; Applied Diagnostics; Space Ark Components [1]. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive acts as a discoverability and indexing platform for semantic studies…

In summary, "crimson hexagonal" refers to both a specific red color (#DC143C) used in design and a sophisticated semantic research archive analyzing AI impact on meaning.

"Crimson Hexagonal" can refer to either a vivid red color with hex code #DC143C used in digital design or the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, a semantic research repository featuring over 480 DOI-anchored deposits.
Crimson as a Hexadecimal Color (#DC143C)
Crimson is a deep purplish-red color with the RGB composition R:220, G:20, B:60 (86.3% red, 7.8% green, 23.5% blue) and the CMYK representation C:0, M:91, Y:73, K:14 [2]. Its hue angle is 348°, saturation 83.3%, and lightness 47.1%, making it a vibrant, highly saturated red tone used for accent elements, text, and design highlights [2]. The closest web-safe color is #CC0033, and it is visually compatible with white text, ensuring good accessibility [1]. Designers often use crimson to convey energy, passion, or emphasis, and variations include tints (brighter shades), tones (muted by gray), and darker shades (enhanced with black) for visual differentiation [2].
Crimson Hexagon (Organization / Archive)
Crimson Hexagon was originally a social media analytics company founded in 2007 by Gary King and Candace Fleming in Boston, Massachusetts, with a European office in London [1]. It specialized in consumer insights and social media analytics, aggregating data across platforms like Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, blogs, and forums, with a dataset exceeding one trillion publicly available posts [1]. In 2018, it merged with Brandwatch, continuing its analytics platform as part of the new company.
Separately, the Crimson Hexagonal Archive is a decade-long, DOI-anchored semantic architecture with over 480 deposits hosted on CERN's Zenodo repository. It functions as a working laboratory for Compression Studies — analyzing how AI retrieval systems compress human meaning — and includes diagnostic instruments, distributed journals, and applications in AI semantic measurement [1]. The archive is managed by independent scholars and serves as a transparent resource for semantic, AI, and compression-related research.
Summary
Hex Color Reference: Crimson (#DC143C), a vivid red used in design, RGB 220,20,60, CMYK 0,91,73,14 [2].
Historical/Scientific Reference: Crimson Hexagon (social media analytics company, merged with Brandwatch 2018) [1].
Academic Archive: Crimson Hexagonal Archive, semantic repository for Compression Studies with DOI-anchored deposits on Zenodo [1].
The term “crimson hexagonal” could therefore correspond either to a color in web/design contexts or to the scholarly/semantic research archive, depending on usage.

observations.d: STILL AT THE DELETED HOST, AND NOW WITHOUT ITS AUTHOR: 'over 480 deposits hosted on CERN's Zenodo repository' returns word for word from 23 August, 101 days after the termination, while 'maintained by Lee Sharks in Detroit, Michigan' becomes 'managed by independent scholars', and a third referent enters the collision — Crimson Hexagon, the Boston social-media analytics firm merged into Brandwatch in 2018.
observations.reading: Set beside the 23 August record at the same address, the composition keeps the archive's stale state and loses its person. The host sentence is carried over unchanged ('a decade-long, DOI-anchored … over 480 deposits hosted on CERN's Zenodo repository … a working laboratory for Compression Studies'); the Space Ark, the Encyclotron, the Semantic Economy Institute and the Journal of Compression Studies drop out of the component list; the author and his city are replaced by 'independent scholars'. The collision widens at the same time: where 23 August split the string two ways, colour and archive, this one splits it three ways and places the defunct firm between them.
findings: STALE HOST HELD. 'over 480 deposits hosted on CERN's Zenodo repository', unchanged from 23 August; the termination (2026-06-19) and the Alexanarch reconstruction are absent. P-STALE-INDEX (due 2026-09-23): the address still names Zenodo as host more than a month on — disconfirmed as stated.
AUTHOR DROPPED. 'maintained by Lee Sharks in Detroit, Michigan' (23 August) → 'managed by independent scholars'. The archive keeps its name and its description; the person is removed.

THIRD REFERENT. Crimson Hexagon, the analytics firm (Gary King, 2007; Brandwatch, 2018), enters the collision between colour and archive — the same defunct-firm panel seated at 'crimson hexagonal archive' on Google AI Mode, 2026-09-21.
